about.message: Cleans out leftover subtitles, .nfo files and other junk your media library no longer needs.
about.description: Short description of the TidyIt extension shown in settings. DO NOT translate file extensions such as '.nfo'.

description.message:
Media apps such as Plex and KODI only delete the video itself, leaving
its subtitles, .nfo files and artwork behind. TidyIt finds folders and
files like these that no longer belong to a video and cleans them up.

It runs in Preview mode by default, which only logs what it would do.
Check the log before switching to Delete or Move.
description.description: Full description of the extension shown in settings. DO NOT translate 'TidyIt', 'Plex', 'KODI', '.nfo' or the mode names 'Preview', 'Delete' and 'Move'.

requirements.message: This extension requires Python 3.8 or newer.
requirements.description: System requirements (each requirement is a separate string). DO NOT translate technical version strings (e.g., Python 3.8.x).

mode_desc.message:
TidyIt Mode.

Identify the TidyIt Mode you want to run in:
 Preview    - Log all planned TidyIt actions, but do not actually perform
              them. This is the absolute safest mode to survey things with
              first.
 Delete     - This handles all of the actual tidying of content. Items
              flagged to be handled are removed in this mode.
 Move       - This mode is similar to Delete except content is moved to
              the location you specify. This allows you to preview/review
              the content and manually remove it yourself on your own.
              The content moved preserves the directory structure it was
              found as (relative to the search path you specified).

This script's primary function is to handle the content you've identified to
be tidied in some way or another. Ideally you'll set this script in Preview
mode and use the logs to determine your level of satisfaction. Once you're
comfortable with how it's behaving, you can flip the mode to one that will
actually be more productive (basically any mode but Preview).

I take absolutely no responsibility for any loss of data sustained to your
system from ill configuration by your part.

NOTE: that you should ALWAYS operate in 'Preview' mode first to confirm
      that the script doesn't cause irreversible damage to your media library.
mode_desc.description: Help text for the Mode option in TidyIt. DO NOT translate the mode names 'Preview', 'Delete' and 'Move' as they are fixed option values. Keep the column layout of the mode list. DO NOT translate the exact uppercase label (NOTE) as it is used to render UI badges.

movepath_desc.message:
Move Path.

This argument is only required if you set your Mode to 'Move'. Identify
the path you want to move handled content to. If no path is specified then
the 'Move' mode falls gracefully back into the 'Preview' mode. The tilde
(~) can be used to expand the path in efforts to support the home
directory, and ${DestDir} is NZBGet's own download folder.
Leave it empty to stay in Preview mode (nothing is moved).
movepath_desc.description: Help text for the MovePath option in TidyIt. DO NOT translate the mode names 'Move' and 'Preview', the tilde (~) or ${DestDir}. DO NOT translate 'NZBGet'.

alwaystrash_desc.message:
Always Trash File Extensions.

Identify the files extensions you want to always throw away if matched.
This is intentionally left blank because the script works fine without it.
But if your video library gets populated with content you'd prefer
not have around, you can identify it here.

Use a 'question mark' (?) to identify single placeholders for
printable characters (this does not include white space). This list is not
case-sensitive. You can also use an 'asterisk' (*) to identify the regular
expression (.*) or zero or many.  Keep in mind that *.nfo is the same as
writing .nfo below.  the * is automatically implied at the front. Use a
comma (,) and/or space to separate more than one entry.
Example=.zip,.r??,.z7,.0??,.1??,.2??,.3??
Leave it empty to trash nothing extra.
alwaystrash_desc.description: Help text for the AlwaysTrash option in TidyIt. DO NOT translate wildcard patterns or file extensions (e.g., *.nfo, .nfo, (.*)). DO NOT translate the example value after 'Example='.

metacontent_desc.message:
Meta Content.

Identify metafile content you wish to handle when they're the only things
left in the video directory.  For example... Microsoft likes putting
a Thumbs.db file which contains a thumbnail cache of any images and videos
found. These are not necessarily useless to us while our media directory
is populated with content, but is utterly useless to us if it isn't.

We want to identify meta content here. There is some common meta information
automatically defined (and do not have to be specified):
- Thumbs.db: Microsoft Thumbnail Database.
- .DS_Store: OSX meta directory.
- .AppleDouble: OSX meta directory.
- __MACOSX: OSX meta directory.
- @eaDir: Synology meta directory.

But you can additionally identify more entries here. Use a comma and/or
space to delimit multiple entries.
Leave it empty to use just the entries above.
metacontent_desc.description: Help text for the MetaContent option in TidyIt. DO NOT translate the file and folder names (Thumbs.db, .DS_Store, .AppleDouble, __MACOSX, @eaDir) or product names (Microsoft, OSX, Synology).

videopaths_desc.message:
Video Libraries to Scan.

Specify any number of directories this script can (recursively) check
delimited by a comma and/or space. ie: /home/nuxref/mystuff, /path/no3, etc
For windows users, you can specify: C:\My Downloads, \\My\Network\Path, etc
This is the only option you have to fill in.
videopaths_desc.description: Help text for the VideoPaths option in TidyIt. DO NOT translate the example paths.

videoextras_desc.message:
Video Extra File Extensions.

Identify the extra files you keep around with your video files. The script
will scan for these files explicitly and remove them if a video file
bearing the same name is not found.  For this reason you do not want to
specify video extensions here.

You can use a 'question mark' (?) to identify single placeholders for
printable characters (this does not include white space). This list is not
case-sensitive. You can also use an 'asterisk' (*) to identify the regular
expression (.*) or zero or many.  Keep in mind that *.nfo is the same as
writing .nfo below.  the * is automatically implied at the front. Use a
comma (,) and/or space to separate more than one entry.

Common extras (.nfo, .srt, .??.srt, .sub, .idx, .txt, .jpg, .tbn and so
on) are always handled, so don't add them here. Listing them again can
make TidyIt mistake a subtitle such as Movie.en.srt for a leftover.
Leave it empty to handle just the common extras.
videoextras_desc.description: Help text for the VideoExtras option in TidyIt. DO NOT translate wildcard patterns, file extensions or file names (e.g., *.nfo, .??.srt, Movie.en.srt). DO NOT translate 'TidyIt'.

videominsize_desc.message:
Minimum Video Size.

Identify the minimum size (in MB) a video file must be before it's
treated as part of your collection (and not a sample or extra).
If you want every video file to be considered equal; simply set
this value to zero (0).
Leave it empty to use the default (150).
videominsize_desc.description: Help text for the VideoMinSize option in TidyIt. Keep the unit 'MB' as is.

processminage_desc.message:
Minimum Processing Age.

Identify the minimum age (in seconds) a file and/or directory can be
before it's processed.  This prevents this script from invading a directory
that may be being concurrently managed by another application around the
same time.  Anything older than 10 Min (600) is relatively safe.
The default is 3600 (1 hour) for an extra precautionary sake.
Set this value to zero (0) if you don't want to factor in
the age of the files and directories scanned.
Leave it empty to use the default (3600).
processminage_desc.description: Help text for the ProcessMinAge option in TidyIt. Keep the numbers as they are.

videoextensions_desc.message:
File extensions for video files.

Only files with these extensions are considered a video. Extensions must
be separated with commas.
Example=.mkv,.avi,.divx,.xvid,.mov,.wmv,.mp4,.mpg,.mpeg,.vob,.iso
Leave it empty to use the example list above.
videoextensions_desc.description: Help text for the VideoExtensions option in TidyIt. DO NOT translate file extensions. DO NOT translate the example value after 'Example='.

safeentries_desc.message:
Tidy Safe Entries.

No doubt there will be a situation where you will point the tidy script
to a series of directories to which you want to intentionally avoid
removing.  Use a comma to identify any content that immediately makes
a directory safe from removal if found. You can specify directory or
filenames. Simply use a comma and/or space to delimit multiple safe
entries.
Leave it empty to use the defaults (.notidy and .tidysafe).
safeentries_desc.description: Help text for the SafeEntries option in TidyIt. DO NOT translate the file names '.notidy' and '.tidysafe'.

keepdirectories_desc.message:
Keep Directories.

Set this to Yes if you want this script to avoid cleaning up directories
during its tidying phases. This option will not apply to meta
directories though.
keepdirectories_desc.description: Help text for the KeepDirectories option in TidyIt. DO NOT translate the fixed value 'Yes'.

debug_desc.message:
Enable debug logging.

If you experience a problem, you can bet I'll have a much easier time solving
it for you if your logs include debugging.  This can be made possible by
flipping this flag here.
debug_desc.description: Help text for the Debug option in TidyIt.

dotidy_desc.message: Tidy the video libraries defined above right now.
dotidy_desc.description: Help text for the DoTidy command in TidyIt.
